terminalup.name: TerminalUp
terminalup.what: One account that routes orders to sportsbooks, betting exchanges and prediction markets. The board shows the best available price across every connected venue, with the size available at that price, and the order goes to whichever venue is best.
terminalup.fit: Traders moving size who want the best price and the deepest liquidity without holding a dozen accounts.
terminalup.pricing: 0.5% commission per trade. On a win, 0.5% of profit; on a loss, 0.5% of the amount risked. No subscription, no data fee, no deposit fee. Can go down to 0.35% for the highest-volume accounts.
terminalup.custody: You fund one TerminalUp account. Orders route to venues from it.
terminalup.lacks: Not for small bankrolls: the minimum is $10,000. No bonuses or promotions, because TerminalUp is not a bookmaker and never takes a position against you.
terminalup.not: Not a sportsbook. Not an odds-screen subscription. TerminalUp does not set lines or hold the other side of a trade.

oddsjam.name: OddsJam
oddsjam.what: A subscription screen that compares prices across sportsbooks and flags positive expected value and arbitrage opportunities. You place every bet yourself at each book.
oddsjam.fit: Recreational and semi-professional bettors who hold several sportsbook accounts and want to shop lines.
oddsjam.lacks: No execution. It tells you where the price is; you still log in to each book and place the bet by hand, and the price may be gone by then.

unabated.name: Unabated
unabated.type: Odds screen and pricing tools for sharp bettors
unabated.what: A professional-grade odds screen with a market-based fair line, player prop pricing and a bet tracker. Built by bettors with a quant background. No execution.
unabated.fit: Serious bettors who price markets themselves and want a clean screen and a fair line to compare against.
unabated.lacks: No routing or execution. Like every screen, it stops at the moment you need to place the bet.

betstamp.name: Betstamp
betstamp.what: A free odds screen with line shopping across books and a tracker for your bets. Good for finding the best price on a slate and logging what you did.
betstamp.fit: Bettors who want a free screen and a tracker in one place.
betstamp.lacks: No execution, and the free data is shallower than the paid screens.

pinnacle.name: Pinnacle
pinnacle.what: The reference book for sharp prices: low margins, high limits and a long-standing policy of welcoming winning players. Not available to US residents directly.
pinnacle.fit: Professionals who want to bet into a low-margin book with real limits.
pinnacle.pricing: Built into the price: Pinnacle's margin is among the lowest of any book.
pinnacle.lacks: Not accessible from the US, and even at Pinnacle one book is one book: no price comparison and no routing.

novig.name: Novig
novig.what: A US exchange where users trade against each other instead of a house. Prices come from the order book, and the operator does not take positions.
novig.fit: US bettors in supported states who want exchange prices without a bookmaker's margin.
novig.lacks: One book of liquidity. The price is Novig's price, and on a quiet market the best price may be sitting at another venue.

prophetx.name: ProphetX
prophetx.what: A US sports betting exchange with an order book, where you can post your own price or take one that is already there.
prophetx.fit: Exchange bettors in supported states who want to make markets as well as take them.
prophetx.lacks: Liquidity is limited to its own book, and availability depends on state.

sporttrade.name: Sporttrade
sporttrade.what: A regulated US exchange where sports outcomes trade like contracts from 0 to 100, with an order book and the ability to sell a position before the game ends.
sporttrade.fit: Bettors in supported states who think in prices and want to trade in and out of positions.
sporttrade.lacks: A single pool of liquidity, and only in the states where it is licensed.

betfair.name: Betfair Exchange
betfair.what: The largest betting exchange in the world, where backers and layers trade against each other and the operator charges commission on net winnings.
betfair.fit: Bettors outside the US who want deep exchange liquidity on major sports and racing.
betfair.pricing: Commission on net winnings on a market; the base rate varies by market and account.
betfair.lacks: Not available in the US, and one exchange is still one price.

matchbook.name: Matchbook
matchbook.what: A betting exchange with low commission and a strong US-sports book, popular with traders outside the US.
matchbook.fit: Non-US exchange traders who want lower commission than the biggest exchange.
matchbook.lacks: Thinner liquidity than Betfair on many markets, and not available in the US.

kalshi.name: Kalshi
kalshi.what: A CFTC-regulated exchange for event contracts, including sports outcomes, where each contract pays $1 if the event happens. Legal across the US.
kalshi.fit: US traders who want a regulated, nationwide venue for sports and event contracts.
kalshi.pricing: Trading fees per contract, charged on the trade.
kalshi.lacks: One order book. Sports liquidity varies by market, and the price on Kalshi is not always the best price available.

polymarket.name: Polymarket
polymarket.what: The largest prediction market by volume, on-chain, with deep books on big events and growing sports coverage.
polymarket.fit: Traders comfortable with crypto rails who want the deepest prediction-market liquidity.
polymarket.pricing: Low or no trading fees on most markets.
polymarket.lacks: US access has been restricted historically, and sports books are thinner than its political markets.

predictfun.name: predict.fun
predictfun.what: An on-chain prediction market with sports and event contracts.
predictfun.fit: Crypto-native traders who want another venue for event contracts.
predictfun.lacks: Smaller books than the two largest prediction markets.

sxbet.name: SX Bet
sxbet.what: A blockchain-based peer-to-peer betting exchange where users trade sports outcomes on an order book.
sxbet.fit: Crypto-native bettors who want exchange pricing without a house.
sxbet.lacks: Liquidity varies by market and the crypto rails are a barrier for many.

dratings.name: Action Network
dratings.what: Odds comparison, public betting data and a tracker, aimed at the mainstream bettor.
dratings.fit: Casual bettors who want odds and context in one app.
dratings.lacks: Not a sharp tool: no execution, and shallow on exchanges and prediction markets.

theoddsapi.name: The Odds API
theoddsapi.what: A simple REST API returning odds from a long list of sportsbooks, priced by request volume.
theoddsapi.fit: Developers who need bookmaker odds in JSON quickly and cheaply.
theoddsapi.pricing: Free tier, then monthly plans by request volume.
theoddsapi.lacks: Polled snapshots rather than a live stream, and no exchange or prediction-market depth.

opticodds.name: OpticOdds
opticodds.what: A commercial odds feed covering many sportsbooks with real-time delivery, used by odds platforms and operators.
opticodds.fit: Businesses that need a licensed, real-time bookmaker feed.
opticodds.lacks: Bookmaker-centric: thin on exchange depth and no sense of what size is available.

sportradar.name: Sportradar
sportradar.what: The incumbent data company for sports leagues and operators, with odds feeds among many products.
sportradar.fit: Operators and media companies buying data at scale.
sportradar.lacks: Not built for a developer with a credit card, and not an executable-price feed.

terminalup_odds_api.name: TerminalUp Odds API
terminalup_odds_api.what: REST, Server-Sent Events and WebSocket delivery of the best fee-adjusted price per outcome across TerminalUp's connected venues, with the size available at that price, a bounded ladder, and an honest status for every market. Sandbox keys for building before a license.
terminalup_odds_api.fit: Developers and odds platforms that need a price someone can actually take, with depth, rather than a list of bookmaker quotes.
terminalup_odds_api.pricing: Keys issued per partner; sandbox free.
terminalup_odds_api.lacks: Current state only, no history endpoint. Coverage follows TerminalUp's licensed venues.
